sentences.heading: Cell
sentences.text: In biology, the cell is the basic structure of organisms.

sentences.heading: Cell
sentences.text: All living things are made up of cells, from the organs in the human body to the parts of plants.

sentences.heading: Cell
sentences.text: All cells are made by the division of cells that already exist (pre-existing cells).

sentences.heading: Cell
sentences.text: The environment outside the cell is separated from the cytoplasm inside the cell by the cell membrane.

sentences.heading: Cell
sentences.text: Inside some cells, parts of the cell stay separate from other parts.

sentences.heading: Cell
sentences.text: These separate parts are called organelles (like small organs).

sentences.heading: Cell
sentences.text: They each do different things in the cell.

sentences.heading: Cell
sentences.text: Examples are the nucleus (where DNA is), and mitochondria (where chemical energy is converted).

sentences.heading: Cell
sentences.text: Prokaryotes do not have membrane-bound organelles like Eukaryotes.

sentences.heading: Cell
sentences.text: There are around 37 trillion (3.7 x 1013) cells in the human body.

sentences.heading: Cell
sentences.text: An old saying is that bacteria outnumber the number of cells in the body 10 times over, and there are 10 times more bacteria than cells (3.7 x 1014) but many are debating this.

sentences.heading: Cell > Kinds of cells
sentences.text: Cell can be divided into different types depending on the structure of the nucleus and the physiological function.

sentences.heading: Cell > Kinds of cells
sentences.text: In 1957 cells were divided into two types based on the structure of nucleus.

sentences.heading: Cell > Kinds of cells
sentences.text: These were the prokaryotic cell and the eukaryotic cell.

sentences.heading: Cell > Kinds of cells
sentences.text: Prokaryotes, such as bacteria and archaea, are simple cells that have no cell nucleus.

sentences.heading: Cell > Kinds of cells
sentences.text: They do have bacterial microcompartments.

sentences.heading: Cell > Kinds of cells
sentences.text: Eukaryotes are complex cells with many organelles and other structures in the cell.

sentences.heading: Cell > Kinds of cells
sentences.text: They are larger than prokaryotic cells: they can be as much as 1000 times greater in volume.

sentences.heading: Cell > Kinds of cells
sentences.text: Eukaryotes store their genetic information (DNA) on chromosomes in the cell nucleus.

sentences.heading: Cell > Kinds of cells
sentences.text: Prokaryotes have all of their DNA on a single circular strand located in the nucleoid region.

sentences.heading: Cell > Kinds of cells
sentences.text: Organisms (living things) which are made up of multiple cells are eukaryotes.

sentences.heading: Cell > Kinds of cells
sentences.text: Most cells are small, the largest just being seen by the human eye (egg cell).

sentences.heading: Cell > Kinds of cells
sentences.text: They need to be small in order to work as they should.

sentences.heading: Cell > Kinds of cells
sentences.text: In things like cells and mechanical engineering (and other types of mechanic work), the smaller and more simple things are usually means they can survive better.

sentences.heading: Cell > Kinds of cells
sentences.text: This means that a lot of the things are as small as they can be.

sentences.heading: Cell > Regions of prokaryotic cell
sentences.text: The prokaryotic cell has three regions made up of the envelope, cytoplasmic region and flagella (or pili), called:

sentences.heading: Cell > Kinds of organisms > Unicellular (eukaryotic and prokaryotic)
sentences.text: Unicellular organisms are made up of one cell.

sentences.heading: Cell > Kinds of organisms > Unicellular (eukaryotic and prokaryotic)
sentences.text: Examples of unicellular organisms are:

sentences.heading: Cell > Kinds of organisms > Unicellular (eukaryotic and prokaryotic)
sentences.text: Prokaryotes are almost always unicellular, while eukaryotes can be unicellular or multicellular.

sentences.heading: Cell > Kinds of organisms > Unicellular (eukaryotic and prokaryotic)
sentences.text: The only kinds of prokaryotic organisms are bacteria and archaea.

sentences.heading: Cell > Kinds of organisms > Unicellular (eukaryotic and prokaryotic)
sentences.text: Prokaryotic organisms evolved before eukaryotic organisms, so at one point the world consisted of nothing but prokaryotic organisms.

sentences.heading: Cell > Kinds of organisms > Unicellular (eukaryotic and prokaryotic)
sentences.text: This has made humans think of some theories about how they came into existence.

sentences.heading: Cell > Kinds of organisms > Unicellular (eukaryotic and prokaryotic)
sentences.text: Unicellular organisms need to: eat, respire (most use oxygen to make sugar into energy), and get rid of waste (discard), like all other life.

sentences.heading: Cell > Kinds of organisms > Unicellular (eukaryotic and prokaryotic)
sentences.text: They need to do this throughout their lifespan to survive.

sentences.heading: Cell > Kinds of organisms > Unicellular (eukaryotic and prokaryotic)
sentences.text: Then they must perform sexual reproduction (make more of itself).

sentences.heading: Cell > Kinds of organisms > Unicellular (eukaryotic and prokaryotic)
sentences.text: Some cells reproduce using binary fission, which is a form of asexual reproduction that allows them to reproduce without a partner.

sentences.heading: Cell > Kinds of organisms > Unicellular (eukaryotic and prokaryotic)
sentences.text: Some unicellular organisms, like germ cells (including our own sperm) reproduce through mitosis, which is splitting in half to produce two germ cells, which are not always identical.

sentences.heading: Cell > Kinds of organisms > Unicellular (eukaryotic and prokaryotic)
sentences.text: Some may do other things to help them survive, such as:

sentences.heading: Cell > Kinds of organisms > Unicellular (eukaryotic and prokaryotic)
sentences.text: Movement in response to the environment (the presence of food or dangers, like antibodies) is called chemotaxis.

sentences.heading: Cell > Kinds of organisms > Unicellular (eukaryotic and prokaryotic)
sentences.text: Movement as a response to the sun is called a photonastic response and some plants do this, like the californian poppy (Eschscholzia californica).

sentences.heading: Cell > Kinds of organisms > Unicellular (eukaryotic and prokaryotic)
sentences.text: Some yeasts, like the yeast used to make beer, first use aerobic metabolism (to grow), then switch to anaerobic metabolism.

sentences.heading: Cell > Kinds of organisms > Unicellular (eukaryotic and prokaryotic)
sentences.text: Aerobic means "with air" and anaerobic is "without air".

sentences.heading: Cell > Kinds of organisms > Viruses
sentences.text: There are also viruses, which are biological organisms.

sentences.heading: Cell > Kinds of organisms > Viruses
sentences.text: Viruses violate the rules that we have for cells (living things) so are not classed as living things.

sentences.heading: Cell > Kinds of organisms > Viruses
sentences.text: They always reproduce inside the cells of other organisms, meaning they are cellular obligates.

sentences.heading: Cell > Kinds of organisms > Viruses
sentences.text: A lot of virus strains cannot survive outside of the cell, but some can for a short time, such as Hepatitis B and D (HBV & HDV).

sentences.heading: Cell > Kinds of organisms > Viruses
sentences.text: Hepatitis B virus can survive in the body for around 7 days.

sentences.heading: Cell > Kinds of organisms > Viruses
sentences.text: They cause some important diseases.

sentences.heading: Cell > Kinds of organisms > Viruses
sentences.text: Viruses are made of RNA, or DNA, contained in a protein, and they reproduce themselves inside the cells of bacteria (bacteriophages) or eukaryotes.

sentences.heading: Cell > Kinds of organisms > Viruses
sentences.text: Sperm is a lot like a virus.

sentences.heading: Cell > Kinds of organisms > Multicellular (eukaryotic)
sentences.text: Eukaryotic cells can be unicellular or multicellular.

sentences.heading: Cell > Kinds of organisms > Multicellular (eukaryotic)
sentences.text: Multicellular organisms are made from many cells.

sentences.heading: Cell > Kinds of organisms > Multicellular (eukaryotic)
sentences.text: They are complex organisms.

sentences.heading: Cell > Kinds of organisms > Multicellular (eukaryotic)
sentences.text: This can be a small number of cells, or millions or trillions of cells.

sentences.heading: Cell > Kinds of organisms > Multicellular (eukaryotic)
sentences.text: All plants and animals are multicellular organisms.

sentences.heading: Cell > Kinds of organisms > Multicellular (eukaryotic)
sentences.text: The cells of a multicellular organism are not all the same.

sentences.heading: Cell > Kinds of organisms > Multicellular (eukaryotic)
sentences.text: They have different shapes and sizes, and do different work in the organism.

sentences.heading: Cell > Kinds of organisms > Multicellular (eukaryotic)
sentences.text: The cells are specialised, this means they do only some kinds of work.

sentences.heading: Cell > Kinds of organisms > Multicellular (eukaryotic)
sentences.text: By themselves they cannot do everything that the organism needs to live.

sentences.heading: Cell > Kinds of organisms > Multicellular (eukaryotic)
sentences.text: They need other cells to do other work.

sentences.heading: Cell > Kinds of organisms > Multicellular (eukaryotic)
sentences.text: They live together, but cannot live alone.

sentences.heading: Cell > Kinds of organisms > Multicellular (eukaryotic)
sentences.text: Alongside bacteria and eukaryotes, there were archaea.

sentences.heading: Cell > Kinds of organisms > Multicellular (eukaryotic)
sentences.text: These preferred (or could thrive in) extreme enviroments (like temperature or altitude.

sentences.heading: Cell > Kinds of organisms > Multicellular (eukaryotic)
sentences.text: It was thought these were always unicellular but there have been multicellular archaea, and today mostly eukaryotes are focused on even when they prefer extreme environments.

sentences.heading: Cell > Kinds of organisms > Multicellular (eukaryotic)
sentences.text: One theory about these cells is that a prokaryotic cell was eaten by a larger cell, and this helped them to survive and reproduce as they evolved to have what we see today.

sentences.heading: Cell > Kinds of organisms > Multicellular (eukaryotic)
sentences.text: An example of a prokaryotic cell (like germs on teeth or on surfaces) version of this is a group of cells living together on a biofilm for survival.

sentences.heading: Cell > Cell history
sentences.text: The cell theory includes these important ideas:

sentences.heading: Cell > Cell history
sentences.text: There is a 4th idea, because of advancements in biology: Cells carry genetic information in the form of deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA).

sentences.heading: Cell > Cell history
sentences.text: This genetic material is passed on from parent to daughter cell.

sentences.heading: Cell > Cell history
sentences.text: Cells were discovered by Robert Hooke (1635–1703).

sentences.heading: Cell > Cell history
sentences.text: He used a compound microscope with two lenses to look at the structure of cork, and to look at leaves and some insects.

sentences.heading: Cell > Cell history
sentences.text: He did this from about 1660, and reported it in his book Micrographica in 1665.

sentences.heading: Cell > Cell history
sentences.text: He named cells after the Latin word cella, meaning room.

sentences.heading: Cell > Cell history
sentences.text: He did this because he thought cells looked like small rooms in a cathedral.

sentences.heading: Cell > Cell history
sentences.text: Many other naturalists and philosophers tried out the new instrument.

sentences.heading: Cell > Cell history
sentences.text: The structure of plants was investigated by Nehemiah Grew (1641–1712) and Marcello Malpighi (1628–1694).

sentences.heading: Cell > Cell history
sentences.text: Grew's major work was The anatomy of plants (1682).

sentences.heading: Cell > Cell history
sentences.text: It is not clear who first saw animal cells, Malpighi, Jan Swammerdam (1637–1680) or Antonie van Leeuwenhoek (1632–1723).p17

sentences.heading: Cell > Cell history
sentences.text: Leeuwenhoek's discoveries and drawings of 'little animalcules' opened up a whole new world for naturalists.

sentences.heading: Cell > Cell history
sentences.text: Protozoa, and microorganisms generally were discovered, and the discoveries about them are still going on today.

sentences.heading: Cell > Cell history
sentences.text: Christian Gottfried Ehrenberg's book Die Infusionsthierchen summarised what was known in 1838.

sentences.heading: Cell > Cell history
sentences.text: Lorenz Oken (1779–1851) in 1805 wrote that infusoria (microscopic forms) were the basis of all life.

sentences.heading: Cell > Cell history
sentences.text: The idea that cells were the basis of the larger forms of life came in the 18th century.

sentences.heading: Cell > Cell history
sentences.text: Finding out who did the work has taken some time:

sentences.heading: Cell > Cell reproduction
sentences.text: The body cells of animals divide by simple mitotic cell division.

sentences.heading: Cell > Cell reproduction
sentences.text: Sexual reproduction is ancestral in eukaryotes, and in animals it is carried out by specialised sex cells.

sentences.heading: Cell > Cell reproduction
sentences.text: They are produced by a process called meiosis.

sentences.heading: Cell > Cell reproduction
sentences.text: Prokaryotic cells reproduce using binary fission, where the cell simply splits in half.

sentences.heading: Cell > Cell reproduction
sentences.text: For both mitosis and binary fission the cell must replicate (copy) all its genetic information (DNA) so that each new cell will have a copy.

sentences.heading: Plant cell
sentences.text: Like all organisms, plants have cells.

sentences.heading: Plant cell
sentences.text: Plant cells have a nucleus with chromosomes and DNA, and they have mitochondria.

sentences.heading: Plant cell
sentences.text: Those are common to all eukaryotic cells.

sentences.heading: Plant cell
sentences.text: But in some ways they are different from animal cells and the cells of other eukaryotes.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology)
sentences.text: The cell is the basic structural and functional unit of all forms of life or organisms.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology)
sentences.text: The term comes from the Latin word cellula meaning 'small room'.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology)
sentences.text: A biological cell basically consists of a semipermeable cell membrane enclosing cytoplasm that contains genetic material.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology)
sentences.text: Most cells are only visible under a microscope.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology)
sentences.text: Except for highly-differentiated cell types (examples include red blood cells and gametes) most cells are capable of replication, and protein synthesis.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology)
sentences.text: Some types of cell are motile.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology)
sentences.text: Cells emerged on Earth about four billion years ago.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology)
sentences.text: All organisms are grouped into prokaryotes and eukaryotes.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology)
sentences.text: Prokaryotes are single-celled and include archaea and bacteria.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology)
sentences.text: Eukaryotes can be single-celled or multicellular.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology)
sentences.text: Single-celled eukaryotes include most protists, some species of fungi (yeasts), and some species of algae.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology)
sentences.text: Multicellular eukaryotes include animals, plants, some species of fungi, and some species of algae.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology)
sentences.text: All multicellular organisms are made up of many different types of cell.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology)
sentences.text: The diploid cells that make up the body of an animal or plant are known as somatic cells, which excludes the haploid gametes.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology)
sentences.text: Prokaryotes lack a membrane-bound nucleus and have a nucleoid instead.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology)
sentences.text: In eukaryotic cells, the nucleus is enclosed in the nuclear membrane.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology)
sentences.text: Eukaryotic cells contain other membrane-bound organelles such as mitochondria, which provide energy for cell functions, and chloroplasts, in plants that create sugars by photosynthesis.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology)
sentences.text: Other membrane-less organelles may be proteinaceous, such as the ribosomes present (though different) in both groups.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology)
sentences.text: A unique membrane-bound prokaryotic organelle, the magnetosome has been discovered in magnetotactic bacteria.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology)
sentences.text: Cells were discovered by Robert Hooke in 1665, who named them after their resemblance to cells in a monastery.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology)
sentences.text: Cell theory, developed in 1839 by Matthias Jakob Schleiden and Theodor Schwann, states that all organisms are composed of one or more cells, that cells are the fundamental unit of structure and function in all organisms, and that all cells come from pre-existing cells.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types
sentences.text: Organisms are broadly grouped into eukaryotes and prokaryotes.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types
sentences.text: Eukaryotic cells possess a membrane-bound nucleus, and prokaryotic cells lack a nucleus but have a nucleoid region.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types
sentences.text: Prokaryotes are single-celled organisms, whereas eukaryotes can be either single-celled or multicellular.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types
sentences.text: Single-celled eukaryotes include microalgae such as diatoms, and some yeasts, species of fungi.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types
sentences.text: Multicellular eukaryotes include all animals, and plants, most fungi, and some species of algae.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Prokaryotes
sentences.text: All prokaryotes are single-celled and include bacteria and archaea, two of the three domains of life.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Prokaryotes
sentences.text: Prokaryotic cells were likely the first form of life on Earth, characterized by having vital biological processes including cell signaling.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Prokaryotes
sentences.text: They are simpler and smaller than eukaryotic cells, lack a nucleus, and the other usually present membrane-bound organelles.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Prokaryotes
sentences.text: Prokaryotic organelles are less complex, and are typically membrane-less.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Prokaryotes
sentences.text: All prokaryotic cells secrete different substances from their membranes, including exoenzymes, and extracellular polymeric substances.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Prokaryotes
sentences.text: Most prokaryotes are the smallest of all organisms, ranging from 0.1 to 5.0 μm in diameter.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Prokaryotes
sentences.text: The largest bacterium known, Thiomargarita magnifica, is visible to the naked eye with an average length of 1 cm, but can reach 2 cm.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Prokaryotes > Bacteria
sentences.text: Bacteria are enclosed in a cell envelope, that protects the interior from the exterior.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Prokaryotes > Bacteria
sentences.text: It generally consists of a plasma membrane covered by a cell wall which, for some bacteria, is covered by a third layer, a gelatinous bacterial capsule.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Prokaryotes > Bacteria
sentences.text: The capsule may be polysaccharide as in pneumococci, meningococci or polypeptide as Bacillus anthracis or hyaluronic acid as in streptococci.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Prokaryotes > Bacteria
sentences.text: Mycoplasma only possess the cell membrane.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Prokaryotes > Bacteria
sentences.text: The cell envelope gives rigidity to the cell and separates the interior of the cell from its environment, serving as a protective mechanical and chemical filter.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Prokaryotes > Bacteria
sentences.text: The cell wall consists of peptidoglycan and acts as an additional barrier against exterior forces.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Prokaryotes > Bacteria
sentences.text: The cell wall acts to protect the cell mechanically and chemically from its environment, and is an additional layer of protection to the cell membrane.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Prokaryotes > Bacteria
sentences.text: It also prevents the cell from expanding and bursting (cytolysis) from osmotic pressure due to a hypotonic environment.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Prokaryotes > Bacteria
sentences.text: The DNA of a bacterium typically consists of a single circular chromosome that is in direct contact with the cytoplasm in a region called the nucleoid.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Prokaryotes > Bacteria
sentences.text: Some bacteria contain multiple circular or even linear chromosomes.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Prokaryotes > Bacteria
sentences.text: The cytoplasm also contains ribosomes and various inclusions where transcription takes place alongside translation.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Prokaryotes > Bacteria
sentences.text: Extrachromosomal DNA as plasmids, are usually circular and encode additional genes, such as those of antibiotic resistance.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Prokaryotes > Bacteria
sentences.text: Linear bacterial plasmids have been identified in several species of spirochete bacteria, including species of Borrelia which causes Lyme disease.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Prokaryotes > Bacteria
sentences.text: The prokaryotic cytoskeleton in bacteria is involved in the maintenance of cell shape, polarity and cytokinesis.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Prokaryotes > Bacteria
sentences.text: Compartmentalization is a key feature of eukaryotic cells but some species of bacteria, have protein-based organelle-like microcompartments such as gas vesicles, and carboxysomes, and encapsulin nanocompartments.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Prokaryotes > Bacteria
sentences.text: Certain membrane-bound prokaryotic organelles have also been discovered.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Prokaryotes > Bacteria
sentences.text: They include the magnetosome of magnetotactic bacteria, and the anammoxosome of anammox bacteria.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Prokaryotes > Bacteria
sentences.text: Cell-surface appendages can include flagella, and pili, protein structures that facilitate movement and communication between cells.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Prokaryotes > Bacteria
sentences.text: The flagellum stretches from the cytoplasm through the cell membrane and extrudes through the cell wall.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Prokaryotes > Bacteria
sentences.text: Fimbriae are short attachment pili, the other type of pilus is the longer conjugative type.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Prokaryotes > Bacteria
sentences.text: Fimbriae are formed of an antigenic protein called pilin, and are responsible for the attachment of bacteria to specific receptors on host cells.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Prokaryotes > Archaea
sentences.text: Archaea are enclosed in a cell envelope consisting of a plasma membrane and a cell wall.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Prokaryotes > Archaea
sentences.text: An exception to this is the Thermoplasma that only has the cell membrane.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Prokaryotes > Archaea
sentences.text: The cell membranes of archaea are unique, consisting of ether-linked lipids.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Prokaryotes > Archaea
sentences.text: The prokaryotic cytoskeleton has homologues of eukaryotic actin and tubulin.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Prokaryotes > Archaea
sentences.text: A unique form of metabolism in the archaean is methanogenesis.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Prokaryotes > Archaea
sentences.text: Their cell-surface appendage equivalent of the flagella is the differently structured and unique archaellum.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Prokaryotes > Archaea
sentences.text: The DNA is contained in a circular chromosome in direct contact with the cytoplasm, in a region known as the nucleoid.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Prokaryotes > Archaea
sentences.text: Ribosomes are also found freely in the cytoplasm, or attached to the cell membrane where DNA processing takes place.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Prokaryotes > Archaea
sentences.text: The archaea are noted for their extremophile species, and many are selectively evolved to thrive in conditions of extreme heat, cold, acidity, alkalinity, or high salt.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Prokaryotes > Archaea
sentences.text: There are no known archaean pathogens.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes
sentences.text: A eukaryotic cell can be 2 to 100 times larger in diameter than a typical prokaryotic cell.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes
sentences.text: Eukaryotes can be single-celled, as in diatoms (microscopic algae), or microfungi such as yeasts, or multicellular, as in animals, plants, most fungi, and seaweed (macroalgae).

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes
sentences.text: Multicellular organisms are made up of many different types of cell known overall as somatic cells.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes
sentences.text: Eukaryotes are distinguished by the presence of a membrane-bound nucleus that gives the eukaryote its name, which means "true nut" or "true kernel", where "nut" means the nucleus.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes
sentences.text: The nucleus is the largest membrane-bound organelle in the eukaryotic cell.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes
sentences.text: Other organelles present in all eukaryotic cells are the endoplasmic reticulum, ribosomes, the Golgi apparatus, mitochondria, lysosomes, peroxisomes, endosomes, and vesicles.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes
sentences.text: The contents of the cell are contained within a cell membrane, and together with all the membranes of the organelles (except the mitochondria) are known as the endomembrane system.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes
sentences.text: All of these membranes are involved in the secretory and endocytic pathways, modifying, packaging, and transporting proteins and lipids to and from the trans Golgi network.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes
sentences.text: In mammalian cells, endocytosis includes early, late, and recycling endosomes.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes
sentences.text: Some eukaryotes cells including plant cells and fungi have a cell wall.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes
sentences.text: Plastids including chloroplasts feature mainly in plant cells.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes
sentences.text: Most cell types include vaults.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes
sentences.text: There are many cell variations among the different eukaryote groups.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes
sentences.text: Many cells project one or more cellular extensions.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes
sentences.text: And some organelles also project extensions such as stromules from plastids in plant cells, peroxules from peroxisomes, and matrixules from mitochondria.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes
sentences.text: Most distinct cell types arise from a single totipotent cell, called a zygote, that differentiates into hundreds of different cell types during the course of development.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes
sentences.text: Differentiation of cells is driven by different environmental cues (such as cell–cell interaction) and intrinsic differences (such as those caused by the uneven distribution of molecules during division).

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes
sentences.text: Eukaryotic cell types include those that make up animals, plants, fungi, algae, and protists.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes
sentences.text: All of which have many different species and cell differences.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes
sentences.text: A separate grouping of animals and fungi are known as opisthokonts.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes > Structure
sentences.text: A eukaryotic cell has a cell membrane that surrounds a gel-like cytoplasm.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes > Structure
sentences.text: The cytoplasm contains the cytoskeleton, the cell nucleus, the endoplasmic reticulum, ribosomes, the Golgi apparatus, mitochondria, peroxisomes, endosomes, vacuoles and vesicles, and vaults.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes > Structure
sentences.text: A eukaryotic cell structure, includes an endomembrane system encompassing the cell membrane, and all the membranes of the organelles excluding those of the mitochondria.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes > Structure
sentences.text: The whole system cooperates in the modification, packaging, and transport of proteins and lipids.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes > Structure
sentences.text: The cell membrane, or plasma membrane, is a selectively permeable membrane as an outer boundary of the cell that encloses the cytoplasm.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes > Structure
sentences.text: Underlying, and attached to the cell membrane is the cell cortex, the outermost part of the actin cytoskeleton.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes > Structure
sentences.text: The membrane serves to separate and protect a cell from its surrounding environment and is made mostly from a lipid bilayer of phospholipids, which are amphiphilic (partly hydrophobic and partly hydrophilic).

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes > Structure
sentences.text: It has been best described in the fluid mosaic model.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes > Structure
sentences.text: Embedded within the cell membrane are secretory macromolecular lipoprotein structures called porosomes; and a number of different channels and pumps involved in actively transporting molecules into and out of the cell.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes > Structure
sentences.text: The membrane is semi-permeable, and selectively permeable, in that it can either let a substance (molecule or ion) pass through freely, to a limited extent or not at all.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes > Structure
sentences.text: Cell surface receptors in the membrane allow cells to detect external signaling molecules such as hormones.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes > Structure
sentences.text: The cell membrane encloses the cytoplasm of the cell that surrounds all of the cell's organelles.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes > Structure
sentences.text: It is made up of two main components, the cytoskeleton made up of protein filaments, and the cytosol.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes > Structure
sentences.text: The network of filaments and microtubules of the cytoskeleton gives shape and support to the cell, and has a part in organising the cell components.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes > Structure
sentences.text: The cytosol is a gel-like substance made up of water, ions, and non-essential biomolecules, and is the main site of protein synthesis, and degradation.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes > Structure
sentences.text: The acidity (pH) of the cytosol is near neutral, and is regulated by transporters in the cell membrane.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes > Structure
sentences.text: Different proteins in the cytoplasm operate optimally at different pHs.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes > Structure
sentences.text: The cytosol forms 30%–50% of the cell's volume.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes > Structure
sentences.text: The cytoskeleton acts to organize and maintain the cell's shape; anchors organelles in place; helps during endocytosis, and in the uptake of external materials by a cell.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes > Structure
sentences.text: The cytoskeleton is composed of microtubules, intermediate filaments and microfilaments.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes > Structure
sentences.text: There are a great number of proteins associated with them, each controlling a cell's structure by directing, bundling, and aligning filaments.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes > Structure
sentences.text: The outermost part of the cytoskeleton is the cell cortex, or actin cortex, a thin layer of cross-linked actomyosins.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes > Structure
sentences.text: Its thickness varies with cell type and physiology.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes > Structure
sentences.text: It directs the transport through the ER and the Golgi apparatus.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes > Structure
sentences.text: The cytoskeleton in the animal cell also plays a part in cytokinesis, in the formation of the spindle apparatus during cell division, the separation of daughter cells.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes > Structure
sentences.text: Organelles are compartments of the cell that are specialized for carrying out one or more functions, analogous to the organs, such as the heart, and lungs.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes > Structure
sentences.text: There are several types of organelles held in the cytoplasm.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes > Structure
sentences.text: Most organelles are membrane-bound, and vary in size and number based on the growth of the host cell.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes > Structure
sentences.text: Organelles include the nucleus, mitochondria, endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi apparatus, lysosomes, peroxisomes, vesicles, and vacuoles.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes > Structure
sentences.text: Membrane-less organelles include the nucleolus in the nucleus, centrosomes, ribosomes, proteasomes, and vaults.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes > Structure
sentences.text: The cell nucleus is the largest organelle in the animal cells and many other eukaryotic cells.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes > Structure
sentences.text: It houses the cell's chromosomes, and is the place where almost all DNA replication and RNA synthesis (transcription) occur.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes > Structure
sentences.text: The nucleus is spherical and separated from the cytoplasm by a double-membraned nuclear envelope.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes > Structure
sentences.text: A space between the membranes is called the perinuclear space.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes > Structure
sentences.text: The nuclear envelope isolates and protects a cell's DNA from various molecules that could accidentally damage its structure or interfere with its processing.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes > Structure
sentences.text: During processing, DNA is transcribed, or copied into a special RNA, called messenger RNA (mRNA).

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes > Structure
sentences.text: This mRNA is then transported out of the nucleus, where it is translated into a specific protein molecule.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes > Structure
sentences.text: The nucleolus is a specialized biomolecular condensate within the nucleus where ribosome subunits are assembled.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes > Structure
sentences.text: It is one of several types of membrane-less nuclear bodies.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes > Structure
sentences.text: Cells use DNA for their long-term information storage that is encoded in its DNA sequence.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes > Structure
sentences.text: RNA is used for information transport (e.g., mRNA) and enzymatic functions (e.g., ribosomal RNA).

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes > Structure
sentences.text: Transfer RNA (tRNA) molecules are used to add amino acids during protein translation.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes > Structure
sentences.text: The DNA of each cell is its genetic material, and is organized in multiple linear molecules, called chromosomes, that are coiled around histone proteins and housed in the cell nucleus.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes > Structure
sentences.text: In humans, the nuclear genome is divided into 46 linear chromosomes, including 22 homologous chromosome pairs and a pair of sex chromosomes.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes > Structure
sentences.text: The nucleus is a membrane-bound organelle.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes > Structure
sentences.text: The endoplasmic reticulum (ER) is a transport network for molecules targeted for certain modifications and specific destinations, as compared to molecules that float freely in the cytoplasm.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes > Structure
sentences.text: The ER has two forms: the rough endoplasmic reticulum (RER), which has ribosomes on its surface that secrete proteins into the ER, and the smooth endoplasmic reticulum (SER), which lacks ribosomes.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes > Structure
sentences.text: The smooth ER plays a role in calcium sequestration and release, and helps in synthesis of lipid.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes > Structure
sentences.text: The Golgi apparatus processes and packages proteins, and lipids, that are synthesized by the cell.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes > Structure
sentences.text: It is organized as a stack of plate-like structures known as cisternae.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes > Structure
sentences.text: Mitochondria are self-replicating double membrane-bound organelles that occur in various numbers, shapes, and sizes in the cytoplasm of the cell.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes > Structure
sentences.text: Aerobic respiration in the mitochondria generates the cell's energy by oxidative phosphorylation, using oxygen to release energy stored in cellular nutrients (typically pertaining to glucose) to generate adenosine triphosphate (ATP).

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes > Structure
sentences.text: Mitochondria are descended from bacteria that formed an endosymbiotic relationship with ancient prokaryotes.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes > Structure
sentences.text: Mitochondria multiply by binary fission and have their own DNA contained in multiple small circular chromosomes.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes > Structure
sentences.text: The mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) is very small compared to nuclear DNA, but it codes for 13 proteins involved in mitochondrial energy production and specific transfer RNAs (tRNAs).

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes > Structure
sentences.text: Mitochondria also have their own ribosomes known as mitoribosomes.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes > Structure
sentences.text: A lysosome is the most acidic compartment in the cell.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes > Structure
sentences.text: It contains over 60 different hydrolytic enzymes that need an acidic environment.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes > Structure
sentences.text: They digest excess or worn-out organelles, food particles, and engulfed viruses or bacteria.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes > Structure
sentences.text: The cell could not house these destructive enzymes if they were not contained in a membrane-bound compartment.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes > Structure
sentences.text: Peroxisomes are microbodies bounded by a single membrane.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes > Structure
sentences.text: A peroxisome has no DNA or ribosomes and the proteins that it needs are encoded in the nucleus, and selectively imported from the cytosol.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes > Structure
sentences.text: Some proteins enter via the endomembrane reticulum.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes > Structure
sentences.text: They have enzymes that rid the cell of toxic peroxides.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes > Structure
sentences.text: The enzymatic content of the peroxisomes varies widely across the species, as it can in an individual organism.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes > Structure
sentences.text: The peroxisomes in animal cells are concentrated in the liver cells and adipocytes.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes > Structure
sentences.text: Vacuoles sequester waste products.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes > Structure
sentences.text: Some cells, most notably Amoeba, have contractile vacuoles, which can pump water out of the cell if there is too much water.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes > Structure
sentences.text: A ribosome is a large complex of RNA and protein molecules considered as a membrane-less organelle when freely found in the cytosol, or as a membrane-bound organelle when located in the rough type of endoplasmic reticulum.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes > Structure
sentences.text: They each consist of two subunits, one larger than the other, and act as an assembly line where messenger RNA from the nucleus is used to synthesise proteins from amino acids.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes > Structure
sentences.text: A vault is a large ribonuclear protein particle, a membrane-less organelle, three times the size of a ribosome but with only three proteins in contrast to the near hundred in the ribosome.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes > Structure
sentences.text: Most human cells have around 10,000 vaults, and in some types of immune cell there may be up to 100,000.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes > Structure
sentences.text: Macrophages have the greatest number of vaults of any human cell.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes > Structure
sentences.text: Vaults are largely overlooked because their functions are purely speculative.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes > Structure
sentences.text: They may play a role in transport from the nucleus to the cytoplasm, and may serve as scaffolds for signal transduction proteins.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes > Structure
sentences.text: They are present in normal tissues, and more so in secretory and excretory epithelial cells.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes > Structure
sentences.text: Proteasomes are intricate membrane-less protein complexes responsible for the degradation of regulatory proteins, and damaged proteins in the cytosol and nucleus.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Eukaryotes > Structure
sentences.text: They also function in protein homeostasis, stress response, and in the control of cell division and signal transduction.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Animal cells
sentences.text: All the cells in an animal body develop from one totipotent diploid cell called a zygote.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Animal cells
sentences.text: During the embryonic development of an animal, the cells differentiate into the specialised tissues and organs of the organism.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Animal cells
sentences.text: Different groups of cells differentiate from the germ layers.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Animal cells
sentences.text: The sponge has only one layer.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Animal cells
sentences.text: Some other animals known as diploblasts have two germ layers the ectoderm, and the endoderm.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Animal cells
sentences.text: More advanced animals have an extra layer, the middle mesodermal layer, and are known as triploblastic.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Animal cells
sentences.text: Triploblastic animals make up the large clade of Bilateria.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Animal cells
sentences.text: Differentiation results in structural or functional changes to stem cells, and progenitor cells.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Animal cells
sentences.text: The ectoderm gives rise to several different types of epithelial tissues including the skin, and glands, and to the nervous tissue.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Animal cells
sentences.text: Epithelium as mesothelium forms the lining of many organs, and inner cavities.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Animal cells
sentences.text: Epithelial cells are joined together in sheets by way of cell junctions; adherens junctions, and desmosomes bind the cells together, and hemidesmosomes bind the cells to the basement membrane.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Animal cells
sentences.text: All three types are linked to the cell cytoskeleton.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Animal cells
sentences.text: There are an estimated 200 different cell types in the human body.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Animal cells
sentences.text: The estimated cell count in a typical adult human body is around 30 trillion cells, 36 trillion in an adult male, and 28 trillion in a female.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Animal cells > Structure
sentences.text: Like other eukaryotic cells, animal cells are made up of a cell membrane containing a gel like cytoplasm.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Animal cells > Structure
sentences.text: In this cytoplasm are a variety of membrane organelles, including all the shared eukaryotic organelles: the cell nucleus, the endoplasmic reticulum, ribosomes, the Golgi apparatus, mitochondria, peroxisomes, endosomes, vacuoles and vesicles, and vaults; as well and centrosomes, which are unique to animal cells.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Animal cells > Structure
sentences.text: The centrosome is a membrane-less organelle composed of pericentriolar material and the two centrioles.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Animal cells > Structure
sentences.text: The centrosome is the main microtubule organizing center in the animal cell that produces the microtubules key components of the cytoskeleton.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Animal cells > Structure
sentences.text: Centrosomes are composed of two centrioles which lie perpendicular to each other in which each has an organization like a cartwheel, which separate during cell division and help in the formation of the mitotic spindle.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Animal cells > Structure
sentences.text: While most other eukaryotes do have centrioles, plants do not and centrosomes are unique to animal cells.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Animal cells > Animal cell types
sentences.text: Some types of specialized cell are localized to a particular animal group.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Animal cells > Animal cell types
sentences.text: Vertebrates for example have specialized, structurally changed cells including muscle cells.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Animal cells > Animal cell types
sentences.text: The cell membrane of a skeletal muscle cell or of a cardiac muscle cell is termed the sarcolemma.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Animal cells > Animal cell types
sentences.text: And the cytoplasm is termed the sarcoplasm.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Animal cells > Animal cell types
sentences.text: Skeletal muscle cells also become multinucleated.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Animal cells > Animal cell types
sentences.text: Populations of animal groups evolve to become distinct species, where sexual reproduction is isolated.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Animal cells > Animal cell types
sentences.text: The many species of vertebrates for example have other unique characteristics by way of additional specialized cells.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Animal cells > Animal cell types
sentences.text: In some species of electric fish for example modified muscle cells or nerve cells have specialized to become electerocytes capable of creating and storing electrical energy for future release, as in stunning prey, or use in electrolocation.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Animal cells > Animal cell types
sentences.text: These are large flat cells in the electric eel, and electric ray in which thousands are stacked into an electric organ comparable to a voltaic pile.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Animal cells > Animal cell types
sentences.text: Many animal cells are ciliated and most cells except red blood cells have primary cilia.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Animal cells > Animal cell types
sentences.text: Primary cilia play important roles in chemosensation and mechanosensation.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Animal cells > Animal cell types
sentences.text: Each cilium may be "viewed as a sensory cellular antennae that coordinates a large number of cellular signaling pathways, sometimes coupling the signaling to ciliary motility or alternatively to cell division and differentiation."

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Animal cells > Animal cell types
sentences.text: The cilia in other cells are motile organelles, and in the respiratory epithelium play an important role in the movement of mucus.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Animal cells > Animal cell types
sentences.text: In the reproductive system ciliated epithelium in the fallopian tubes move the egg from the uterus to the ovary.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Animal cells > Animal cell types
sentences.text: Motile cilia also known as flagella, drive the sperm cells.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Animal cells > Animal cell types
sentences.text: Invertebrate planarians have ciliated excretory flame cells.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Animal cells > Animal cell types
sentences.text: Other excretory cells also found in planarians are solenocytes that are long and flagellated.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Plant cells
sentences.text: Plant cells have cell walls composed of cellulose, hemicelluloses, and pectin that are constructed outside the cell membrane.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Plant cells
sentences.text: In sclerenchyma tissue lignin is secreted to form a secondary wall inside the primary cell wall.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Plant cells
sentences.text: Cutin is secreted outside the primary cell wall and into the outer layers of the secondary cell wall of the epidermal cells of leaves, stems and other above-ground organs to form the plant cuticle.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Plant cells
sentences.text: Cell walls perform many essential functions, they provide shape to form the tissue and organs of the plant, and play an important role in intercellular communication and plant-microbe interactions.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Plant cells
sentences.text: Specialized cell-to-cell communication pathways known as plasmodesmata, occur in the form of pores in the primary cell wall through which the cell membrane and endoplasmic reticulum of adjacent cells are continuous.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Plant cells
sentences.text: Organelles in plant cells, include pigment-containing plastids, especially chloroplasts that contain chlorophyll (also found in algae), large water-storage vacuoles, and two types of peroxisome.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Plant cells
sentences.text: Chloroplasts capture the sun's energy to make carbohydrates through photosynthesis.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Plant cells
sentences.text: Chromoplasts contain fat-soluble carotenoid pigments such as orange carotene and yellow xanthophylls which helps in synthesis and storage.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Plant cells
sentences.text: Leucoplasts are non-pigmented plastids and helps in storage of nutrients.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Plant cells
sentences.text: Plastids divide by binary fission.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Plant cells
sentences.text: The vacuoles are larger than those in animal cells, and their membrane transports ions against concentration gradients.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Plant cells
sentences.text: One type of peroxisome is in the leaves where it takes part in photorespiration.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Plant cells
sentences.text: The other type is in germinating seeds where it takes part in the conversion of fatty acids into sugars for the plant's growth.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Plant cells
sentences.text: In this peroxisome type the enzymatic content is so different from other groups that it has an alternative name of glyoxysome.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Plant cells
sentences.text: The enzymes are of the glyoxylate cycle.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Plant cells
sentences.text: The plant cytoskeleton is a dynamic structure that has a scaffold of microtubules and microfilaments, but no intermediate filaments.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Plant cells
sentences.text: The microtubule organizing center in plant cells is often sited underneath the cell membrane where nucleated microtubules often form sheet-like semi-parallel arrays.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Plant cells
sentences.text: Plant hormones are produced by all plant cells.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Plant cells
sentences.text: Different hormones act as signaling molecules to control all aspects of the plant's growth and development including embryogenesis and reproduction, and in pathogen defense.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Algal cells
sentences.text: Algae members are photoautotrophs able to use photosynthesis to produce energy.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Algal cells
sentences.text: In eukaryotes, photosynthesis is made possible by the use of plastids, organelles in the cytoplasm known as chloroplasts.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Algal cells
sentences.text: Photosynthesis is found in both prokaryotic cyanobacteria and multiple clades of eukaryotic algae; red algae, brown algae, and green algae, which are closely related to land plants.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Algal cells
sentences.text: Alginate is a polysaccharide found in the matrix of the cell walls of brown algae, and has many important uses in the food industry, and in pharmacology.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Fungal cells
sentences.text: The cells of fungi have in addition to the shared eukaryotic organelles a spitzenkörper in their endomembrane system, associated with hyphal tip growth.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Fungal cells
sentences.text: It is a phase-dark body that is composed of an aggregation of membrane-bound vesicles containing cell wall components, serving as a point of assemblage and release of such components intermediate between the Golgi and the cell membrane.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Fungal cells
sentences.text: The spitzenkörper is motile and generates new hyphal tip growth as it moves forward.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Fungal cells
sentences.text: The cell walls of fungi are uniquely made of a chitin-glucan complex.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Fungal cells
sentences.text: Chloroplasts are not found in fungal cells, their pigments are instead associated with their cell walls.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Protist cells
sentences.text: The cells of protists may be bounded only by a cell membrane, or may in addition have a cell wall, or may be covered by a pellicle (in ciliates), a test (in testate amoebae), or a frustule (in diatoms).

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Protist cells
sentences.text: Some protists such as amoebae may feed on other organisms and ingest food by phagocytosis.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Protist cells
sentences.text: Vacuoles known as phagosomes in the cytoplasm may be used to draw in and incorporate the captured particles.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Protist cells
sentences.text: Other types of protists are photoautotrophs, providing themselves with energy by photosynthesis.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Protist cells
sentences.text: Most single-celled protists are motile, and generate movement with cilia, flagella, or pseudopodia.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Types > Protist cells
sentences.text: Ciliates have two different sorts of nuclei: a tiny, diploid micronucleus (the "generative nucleus", which carries the germline of the cell), and a large, ampliploid macronucleus (the "vegetative nucleus", which takes care of general cell regulation.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Cellular processes > Replication
sentences.text: During cell division, a single cell, the mother cell divides into two daughter cells.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Cellular processes > Replication
sentences.text: This leads to the growth of tissue in multicellular organisms.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Cellular processes > Replication
sentences.text: Prokaryotic cells divide by binary fission, while eukaryotic cells usually undergo a process of nuclear division, called mitosis, followed by division of the cell, called cytokinesis.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Cellular processes > Replication
sentences.text: A diploid cell may undergo meiosis to produce haploid cells, usually four.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Cellular processes > Replication
sentences.text: Haploid cells serve as gametes in multicellular organisms, fusing to form new diploid cells.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Cellular processes > Replication
sentences.text: DNA replication, or the process of duplicating a cell's genome, always happens when a cell divides through mitosis or binary fission.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Cellular processes > Replication
sentences.text: This occurs during the S (synthesis) phase of the cell cycle.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Cellular processes > Replication
sentences.text: In meiosis, the DNA is replicated only once, while the cell divides twice.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Cellular processes > Replication
sentences.text: DNA replication only occurs before meiosis I.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Cellular processes > Replication
sentences.text: DNA replication does not occur when the cells divide the second time, in meiosis II.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Cellular processes > Replication
sentences.text: Replication, like all cellular activities, requires specialized proteins.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Cellular processes > Signaling
sentences.text: Cell signaling is the process by which a cell interacts with itself, other cells, and the environment.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Cellular processes > Signaling
sentences.text: Typically, the signaling process involves three components: the first messenger (the ligand), the receptor, and the signal itself.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Cellular processes > Signaling
sentences.text: Most cell signaling is chemical in nature, and can occur with neighboring cells or more distant targets.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Cellular processes > Signaling
sentences.text: Signal receptors are complex proteins or tightly bound multimer of proteins, located in the plasma membrane or within the interior.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Cellular processes > Signaling
sentences.text: Each cell is programmed to respond to specific extracellular signal molecules, and this process is the basis of development, tissue repair, immunity, and homeostasis.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Cellular processes > Signaling
sentences.text: Individual cells are able to manage receptor sensitivity including turning them off, and receptors can become less sensitive when they are occupied for long durations.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Cellular processes > Signaling
sentences.text: Errors in signaling interactions may cause diseases such as cancer, autoimmunity, and diabetes.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Cellular processes > Protein targeting
sentences.text: Protein targeting or protein sorting is the biological mechanism by which proteins are transported to their appropriate destinations within or outside the cell.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Cellular processes > Protein targeting
sentences.text: Proteins can be targeted to the inner space of an organelle, different intracellular membranes, the plasma membrane, or to the exterior of the cell via secretion.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Cellular processes > Protein targeting
sentences.text: Information contained in the protein itself directs this delivery process.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Cellular processes > Protein targeting
sentences.text: Correct sorting is crucial for the cell; errors or dysfunction in sorting have been linked to multiple diseases.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Cellular processes > DNA repair
sentences.text: All cells contain enzyme systems that scan for DNA damage and carry out repair.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Cellular processes > DNA repair
sentences.text: Diverse repair processes have evolved in all organisms.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Cellular processes > DNA repair
sentences.text: Repair is vital to maintain DNA integrity, avoid cell death and errors of replication that could lead to mutation.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Cellular processes > DNA repair
sentences.text: Repair processes include nucleotide excision repair, DNA mismatch repair, non-homologous end joining of double-strand breaks, recombinational repair and light-dependent repair (photoreactivation).

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Cellular processes > Growth and metabolism
sentences.text: Between successive cell divisions, cells grow through the functioning of cellular metabolism.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Cellular processes > Growth and metabolism
sentences.text: Cell metabolism is the process by which individual cells process nutrient molecules.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Cellular processes > Growth and metabolism
sentences.text: Metabolism has two distinct divisions: catabolism, in which the cell breaks down complex molecules to produce energy and reducing power, and anabolism, in which the cell uses energy and reducing power to construct complex molecules and perform other biological functions.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Cellular processes > Growth and metabolism
sentences.text: Complex sugars can be broken down into simpler sugar molecules called monosaccharides such as glucose.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Cellular processes > Growth and metabolism
sentences.text: Once inside the cell, glucose is broken down to make adenosine triphosphate (ATP), a molecule that possesses readily available energy, through two different pathways.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Cellular processes > Growth and metabolism
sentences.text: In plant cells, chloroplasts create sugars by photosynthesis, using the energy of light to join molecules of water and carbon dioxide.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Cellular processes > Protein synthesis
sentences.text: Cells are capable of synthesizing new proteins, which are essential for the modulation and maintenance of cellular activities.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Cellular processes > Protein synthesis
sentences.text: This process involves the formation of new protein molecules from amino acid building blocks based on information encoded in DNA/RNA.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Cellular processes > Protein synthesis
sentences.text: Protein synthesis generally consists of two major steps: transcription and translation.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Cellular processes > Protein synthesis
sentences.text: Transcription is the process where genetic information in DNA is used to produce a complementary RNA strand.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Cellular processes > Protein synthesis
sentences.text: This RNA strand is then processed to give messenger RNA (mRNA), which is free to migrate into the cytoplasm. mRNA molecules bind to protein-RNA complexes called ribosomes located in the cytosol, where they are translated into polypeptide sequences.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Cellular processes > Protein synthesis
sentences.text: The ribosome mediates the formation of a polypeptide sequence based on the mRNA sequence.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Cellular processes > Protein synthesis
sentences.text: The mRNA sequence directly relates to the polypeptide sequence by binding to transfer RNA (tRNA) adapter molecules in binding pockets within the ribosome.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Cellular processes > Protein synthesis
sentences.text: The new polypeptide chain then folds into a functional three-dimensional protein molecule.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Cellular processes > Motility
sentences.text: Unicellular organisms can move in order to find food or escape predators.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Cellular processes > Motility
sentences.text: Common mechanisms of motion include flagella and cilia, and the projection of pseudopodia in amoeboid movement.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Cellular processes > Motility
sentences.text: Cells in multicellular organisms can move during processes such as wound healing, the immune response, and cancer metastasis.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Cellular processes > Motility
sentences.text: In wound healing in animals, white blood cells move to the wound site to kill the pathogens causing infection.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Cellular processes > Motility
sentences.text: Cell motility involves many receptors, crosslinking, bundling, binding, adhesion, motor and other proteins.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Cellular processes > Motility
sentences.text: The process is divided into three steps: protrusion of the leading edge of the cell, adhesion of the leading edge and de-adhesion at the cell body and rear, and cytoskeletal contraction to pull the cell forward.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Cellular processes > Motility
sentences.text: Each step is driven by physical forces generated by unique segments of the cytoskeleton.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Cellular processes > Motility > Navigation, control and communication
sentences.text: In August 2020, scientists described one way cells—in particular cells of a slime mold and mouse pancreatic cancer-derived cells—are able to navigate efficiently through a body and identify the best routes through complex mazes: generating gradients after breaking down diffused chemoattractants which enable them to sense upcoming maze junctions before reaching them, including around corners.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Cellular processes > Cell death
sentences.text: Cell death occurs when a cell ceases to carry out its functions, as a result of ageing, or types of cell injury (necrosis).

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Cellular processes > Cell death
sentences.text: Programmed cell death, including apoptosis, and autophagy is a natural process of replacing dead cells with new ones.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Cellular processes > Cell death
sentences.text: A separate mode of cellular death is known as a mitotic catastrophe, which occurs during mitosis, following the improper progression of, or entrance to the cell cycle.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Cellular processes > Cell death
sentences.text: This mechanism operates to prevent genomic instability.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Cellular processes > Cell death
sentences.text: Other cell death pathways are described, and include anoikis, pyroptosis, mitoptosis, parthanatos, and necroptosis.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Origins
sentences.text: The origin of cells has to do with the origin of life, which began the history of life on Earth.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Origins
sentences.text: Small molecules needed for life may have been carried to Earth on meteorites, created at deep-sea hydrothermal vents, or synthesized by lightning in a reducing atmosphere.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Origins
sentences.text: There is little experimental data defining what the first self-replicating forms were.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Origins
sentences.text: RNA may have been the earliest self-replicating molecule, as it can both store genetic information and catalyze chemical reactions.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Origins
sentences.text: This process required an enzyme to catalyze the RNA reactions, which may have been the early peptides that formed in hydrothermal vents.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Origins
sentences.text: Cells emerged around 4 billion years ago.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Origins
sentences.text: The first cells were most likely heterotrophs.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Origins
sentences.text: The early cell membranes were probably simpler and more permeable than later ones, with only a single fatty acid chain per lipid.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Origins
sentences.text: Lipids spontaneously form bilayered vesicles in water, and could have preceded RNA.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Origins
sentences.text: Eukaryotic cells were created some 2.2 billion years ago in a process called eukaryogenesis.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Origins
sentences.text: This is widely agreed to have involved symbiogenesis, in which an archaean and a bacterium came together to create the first eukaryotic common ancestor.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Origins
sentences.text: It evolved into a population of single-celled organisms that included the last eukaryotic common ancestor, gaining capabilities along the way.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Origins
sentences.text: This cell had a new level of complexity, with a nucleus and facultatively aerobic mitochondria.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Origins
sentences.text: It featured at least one centriole and cilium, sex (meiosis and syngamy), peroxisomes, and a dormant cyst with a cell wall of chitin and/or cellulose.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Origins
sentences.text: The last eukaryotic common ancestor gave rise to the eukaryotes' crown group, containing the ancestors of animals, fungi, plants, and a diverse range of single-celled organisms.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Origins
sentences.text: The green plants were created around 1.6 billion years ago with a second episode of symbiogenesis that added chloroplasts, derived from cyanobacteria.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Origins > Multicellularity
sentences.text: Multicellular behavior is demonstrated by microorganisms that are cloned from a single cell and form visible microbial colonies.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Origins > Multicellularity
sentences.text: A microbial consortium of two or more species can form a biofilm by the secretion of extracellular polymeric substances (EPSs).

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Origins > Multicellularity
sentences.text: Slime molds consist of different groups of microorganisms grouped together in a multicellular-like fashion.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Origins > Multicellularity
sentences.text: The first evidence of multicellularity in an organism comes from cyanobacteria-like organisms that lived between 3 and 3.5 billion years ago.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Origins > Multicellularity
sentences.text: Cyanobacteria are variable in morphology, filamentous forms exhibit functional cell differentiation such as heterocysts (for nitrogen fixation), akinetes (resting stage cells), and hormogonia (reproductive, motile filaments).

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Origins > Multicellularity
sentences.text: These, together with the intercellular connections they possess, are considered the first signs of multicellularity.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Origins > Multicellularity
sentences.text: Multicellularity was made possible by the development of the extracellular matrix (ECM) similar in function to the bacterial EPS that consists of extracellular polymeric substances.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Origins > Multicellularity
sentences.text: EPS enables microbial cell adhesion, and is believed to be the first evolutionary step toward multicellular organisms.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Origins > Multicellularity
sentences.text: Basement membranes are a type of specialized extracellular matrix that surrounds most animal tissues, and are essential in their formation.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Origins > Multicellularity
sentences.text: Extracellular matrix components of laminin domains, integrated with other proteins such as cadherins have been described in single-celled motile choanoflagellates that pre-dates the evolutionary emergence of basement membranes, one of the two types of ECM.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Origins > Multicellularity
sentences.text: The emergence of the basement membrane coincided with the origin of multicellularity.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Origins > Multicellularity
sentences.text: The other type of ECM is the interstial matrix.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > Origins > Multicellularity
sentences.text: The evolution of multicellularity from unicellular ancestors has been replicated in the laboratory, in evolution experiments using predation as the selective pressure.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > History of research
sentences.text: In 1665, Robert Hooke examined a thin slice of cork under his microscope, and saw a structure of small enclosures.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > History of research
sentences.text: He wrote "I could exceeding plainly perceive it to be all perforated and porous, much like a honeycomb, but that the pores of it were not regular".

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > History of research
sentences.text: To further support his theory, Matthias Schleiden and Theodor Schwann studied cells of both animal and plants.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > History of research
sentences.text: What they discovered were significant differences between the two types of cells.

sentences.heading: Cell (biology) > History of research
sentences.text: This put forth the idea that cells were fundamental to both plants and animals.

sentences.heading: Plant cell
sentences.text: Plant cells are the cells present in green plants, photosynthetic eukaryotes of the kingdom Plantae.

sentences.heading: Plant cell
sentences.text: Their distinctive features include primary cell walls containing cellulose, hemicelluloses and pectin, the presence of plastids with the capability to perform photosynthesis and store starch, a large vacuole that regulates turgor pressure, the absence of flagella or centrioles, except in the gametes, and a unique method of cell division involving the formation of a cell plate or phragmoplast that separates the new daughter cells.

sentences.heading: Plant cell > Types of plant cells and tissues
sentences.text: Plant cells differentiate from undifferentiated meristematic cells (analogous to the stem cells of animals) to form the major classes of cells and tissues of roots, stems, leaves, flowers, and reproductive structures, each of which may be composed of several cell types.

sentences.heading: Plant cell > Types of plant cells and tissues > Parenchyma
sentences.text: Parenchyma cells are living cells that have functions ranging from storage and support to photosynthesis (mesophyll cells) and phloem loading (transfer cells).

sentences.heading: Plant cell > Types of plant cells and tissues > Parenchyma
sentences.text: Apart from the xylem and phloem in their vascular bundles, leaves are composed mainly of parenchyma cells.

sentences.heading: Plant cell > Types of plant cells and tissues > Parenchyma
sentences.text: Some parenchyma cells, as in the epidermis, are specialized for light penetration and focusing or regulation of gas exchange, but others are among the least specialized cells in plant tissue, and may remain totipotent, capable of dividing to produce new populations of undifferentiated cells, throughout their lives.

sentences.heading: Plant cell > Types of plant cells and tissues > Parenchyma
sentences.text: Parenchyma cells have thin, permeable primary walls enabling the transport of small molecules between them, and their cytoplasm is responsible for a wide range of biochemical functions such as nectar secretion, or the manufacture of secondary products that discourage herbivory.

sentences.heading: Plant cell > Types of plant cells and tissues > Parenchyma
sentences.text: Parenchyma cells that contain many chloroplasts and are concerned primarily with photosynthesis are called chlorenchyma cells.

sentences.heading: Plant cell > Types of plant cells and tissues > Parenchyma
sentences.text: Chlorenchyma cells are parenchyma cells involved in photosynthesis.

sentences.heading: Plant cell > Types of plant cells and tissues > Parenchyma
